text: Jaeha was counting on this. As the doors close on Mok's smile, Borro's huge hand shoots out and grabs his gold chain.
One yank, and Mok comes flying in. The doors slam behind him.
He lands face first at Jaeha's feet. Jaeha looks down at him very politely.
Outside, the sealer drives the stake in without looking, and violet light webs over the doors.
The sealer turns, proud of his work, and asks after his boss. Nobody wants to say it.
The stake's timer starts counting down an hour. That seal was meant for Jaeha.
The sealer can't pull his own stake out. Sora checks her compass and smiles, in no hurry at all.
Inside, Mok pounds on the bronze, roaring at his men. For once, he's on the wrong side of a door.
Nib offers him the doors with an open palm, the way he offers everything.
Nib's face doesn't move. He warned Mok about doors once already, at the memorial.
Mok snatches his radio. He sent two sealers round to shut the other way out.
The answer crackles back, half drowned. Team two trusted the trap-tester's code.
In the crypt, the sealers scramble onto a tomb, chest-deep, the way back already underwater.
The water creeps over Jaeha's chalk arrow, with its tiny extra tick.
Jaeha did as he was told: he marked the way, and they followed. For the first time, Mok looks afraid.
The chamber itself: a flooded dome hung with bells, a stair up to a small high door, and something huge slumped in the middle.
Mok spots the little door high up, and understands. Jaeha never meant to stay trapped. Nib found the way out.
Mok's ugly grin comes back. A back door means he can leave them all behind again.
But the slumped giant is sitting right in front of the stair, and its head is lifting.
The Drowned Bell-Ringer rises: six metres of drowned stone and rusted chain, a cracked bell for a head, a clapper like a tree trunk.
B-grade, and hushed. Ash drifts from the crack down its side.
Mok's grin is gone. He backs up behind his shield, and Jaeha politely asks if he still wants to lead.
Both summons flare into field form, five minutes each. In Borro's moss, a tiny lens watches it all.
The clapper comes down in a huge arc, and Borro steps under it.
It drives him to one knee.
Half of it lands in Jaeha.
Nib shreds its robes and chains, but the stone underneath barely scratches.
Then the giant knocks on its own bell-head.
It tolls, and a ring of force flattens the water and throws everyone off their feet. Everyone but Nib, at its ankle.
Jaeha, bleeding from one ear, stares at Nib, untouched.
That's the trick. The blast begins where the giant's arm ends. Right under it, nothing touches you.
His voice won't survive that toll, so he hands Yerin the chalk and a job by the giant's feet.
He grins through the blood. Traps are the one thing he knows better than anyone.
Yerin runs at the giant, chalk in her fist, with Borro's shield over her head.
She slashes a thick chalk ring round a pillar.
The clapper swings at them, and Borro takes it, sliding.
Mok stays behind his shield, calculating. Once the giant is worn down, the way out is his.
Outside, the stream passes six hundred thousand, and the chat starts asking questions Mok won't like.
In Borro's moss, the drone's red light glows. It's recording all of it.
The giant swings at Jaeha, alone in the open water.
And Mok lunges out, a tank's reflex, throwing his shield over Jaeha.
The blow cracks his shield right through the hound's head.
Carry only works on summons, not on Mok. So Jaeha puts Mok's load onto a summon.
Borro slides his shield in beside Mok's, and the weight spreads across both.
And Jaeha carries ninety percent of what Borro took from Mok. He is carrying Mok, of all people.
Mok feels the weight vanish and can't understand it. Jaeha answers with Minseok's rule, and includes Mok in it.
Something in Mok's eyes cracks, like his shield.
Borro heaves both shields up and throws the clapper off.
Yerin waves them in. She has ringed three pillars in chalk, right under the giant.
They run in close as the giant raises its fist again.
The toll smashes into the walls, but inside the chalk rings the water doesn't ripple. Jaeha drops Borro to rest form to save his clock.
Mok stares at the white line round his boots. A guild full of steel, and the answer was chalk.
Bloody and polite, Jaeha returns a joke Mok's men made on the night they left him to die.
Nib climbs the giant's arm and slashes at the crack in its bell, but the bronze holds.
It swats him away, drops its clapper and clutches its bell-head in both hands, as if in pain.
The crack widens and glows, and the whole bell starts to hum.
Every bell in the dome begins to shiver. Mok asks what's happening. Jaeha knows: no more single tolls.
The window turns red. The giant is enraged, with thirty seconds on the clock.
Ring after ring rolls out without stopping, each starting a little closer. The safe space shrinks.
The walls crack and bulge inward, and pieces of the dome fall.
The stair crumbles, cutting off the door. A small window adds to Jaeha's list: no release, again.
All five are squeezed against one pillar as the safe ring shrinks. Nib's field form is nearly spent, and steel won't cut that bell.
At the edge of his vision, the tiny mark pulses. He said he'd need it in here.
His eyes harden. The decision is made.
Twenty-four seconds. Long enough, maybe, for one phone call.
